sentences.text:
THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -4-  NC: 2023:KHC-D:10789  MFA No. 100499 of 2014  C/W MFA No. 100968 of 2014  JUDGMENT MFA No.100499/2014 is filed by the Insurance company praying to reduce the quantum of compensation.
2. MFA No.100968/2014 is filed by the claimants for enhancement of compensation.
3. The factum of accident, the deceased being student of Bachelor of Engineering died in the accident and liability on the Insurance company are not disputed.
4. In the present case, the deceased was aged 20 years studying Bachelor of Engineering died in the accident.

The Tribunal has held notional income at Rs.8,000/- per month by adding 50% of income towards loss of future prospects in life and deducting 50% of income towards his personal expenses since deceased was Bachelor and applying the appropriate multiplier awarded compensation of Rs.12,96,000/- on the head loss of dependency and awarded sum of Rs.50,000/- towards other conventional NC: 2023:KHC-D:10789 heads like loss of estate, loss of love and care and transportation of dead body funeral and obsequies.
Thus, in all awarded compensation of Rs.13,46,000/- with interest at 8% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
5. The deceased was studying Bachelor of Engineering in Civil Discipline and as future prospects in his career if he is alive.
Therefore, considering the factor that the deceased was Bachelor of Engineering student a minimum income of Rs.12,000/- per month is taken into consideration.

The Tribunal has committed error by adding 50% income towards loss of future prospects in life, since the deceased was still student of engineering and at that time was not having permanent nature of job and income.
Therefore, 40% of income ought to have been added but not 50%.
Since, the deceased was bachelor, 50% of income is deducted towards personal and living expenses.
The appropriate multiplier is 18.

Therefore, loss of dependency is hereby re-assessed and quantified as:
NC: 2023:KHC-D:10789 Rs.12,000 + 4800(40% of 12,000) X 50/100 X 18 X 12 =18,14,400/-

Nagangouda S/O. Venkanagouda Naganur vs Mahadev Swamy S/O. Chikkann on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82871251/
4 6.
There are two dependants.
Hence, Rs.88,000/- is awarded under the loss of consortium (40,000/-X2+10%).
7. Compensation of Rs.15000/- + 10% escalation i.e. Rs.1,500/-.
Total of Rs.16,500/- is awarded under the head loss of estate.
8. Compensation of Rs.15000/- + 10% escalation i.e. Rs.1,500/-.
Total of Rs.16,500/- is awarded under the head loss of estate.

9. Thus, the claimants would be entitled for compensation under various heads as under:
 Sl. Heads.

Amount in  No. (Rs.)
 1. Towards loss of dependency 18,14,420-00  2. Towards loss of consortium 88,000-00  (40,000 x 2 +10%)
 3. Towards loss of estate 16,500,-00  (Rs.15,000 + 10%)
 4. Towards transportation of dead 16,500,-00  body and funeal and obsequies  (Rs.15,000 + 10%)

Therefore, the claimants in MFA No.100499/2014 are entitled for compensation of Rs. 19,35,420-00 as against Rs.13,46,000/-
awarded by the tribunal.

The rate of interest awarded by the tribunal at 8% p.a. is reduced to 6% p.a.
11.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeal filed by the claimants is allowed in part.
ii) The appeal filed by the insurance company is also liable to be allowed in part insofar as addition of income towards loss of future prospects in life and on rate of interest.
Nagangouda S/O. Venkanagouda Naganur vs Mahadev Swamy S/O. Chikkann on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82871251/
5
iii) The judgment and award dated 24.09.2013, passed by the I Addl.
Senior Civil Judge and CJM and AMACT Dharwad sitting at Navalgund, in MVC No.105/2013 stands modified.

NC: 2023:KHC-D:10789 iv) The claimants in MFA No.100499/2014 are entitled for total compensation of Rs. 19,35,420-00 along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization, as against Rs.13,46,000/- awarded by the tribunal.
v) The Insurance company is directed to deposit the award amount within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
vi) The amount in deposit, shall be transmitted to the tribunal forthwith.
vii) No order as to costs.
viii) Draw award accordingly.

SD/-
